title.purpose: The open task's title, two lines at most.

headline.purpose: The panel's name in its header.

body-strong.purpose: A row's key, a station's name, a link chip.

small.purpose: Second lines of rows, station details, metadata, gists.

line-name.purpose: Agentes and Entrega above their rails, in the line's colour.

label.purpose: Uppercase heading of a list or of a folded section.

hint.purpose: The ink tooltip above a station.

mono.purpose: Branches, commits, paths, code and logs.

shadows.name: warm-float
shadows.purpose: Menus, the theme picker and modals that open on top.

shadows.name: station-halo
shadows.purpose: A station under the pointer or with focus, in the station's own colour.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The ink wash behind a modal (a background, listed here with depth).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Curve of the station hover, the hint, overlays and the merge landing (--ease-out).

motion.name: station-hover
motion.purpose: Halo, growth to 1.2, name colour and hint of a stage under the pointer.

motion.name: station-state
motion.purpose: A station changing fill and ring when its stage changes state.

motion.name: merge-landing
motion.purpose: The line draws itself to the Merge station; a fade with reduced motion.

motion.name: queue-arrive
motion.purpose: A row that just came to need the user tints amber once.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: The live dot, only without reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: lines-side-by-side
breakpoints.value: about 1000px for Agentes plus 1120px for Entrega; narrower, the two lines stack

breakpoints.name: station-min
breakpoints.value: 96px per step, 144px per agent stage; narrower, the line wraps

narrative.overview:
Each task is a line and its stages are stations, so where it is and where it stopped is read at a glance. The theme is a transit plan printed on paper: a warm off-white ground, white surfaces, thin warm hairlines, and one coffee-black ink that writes the text, fills the primary button and makes the window bar a solid band. Two flat line colours carry the diagram, blue for Agentes and green for Entrega, and nothing else on the screen is allowed to be decorative colour.

It is a working tool beside an editor, in daylight, read by someone coming back to see what moved. Rows are dense, rules are thin, secondary controls have no box, and state is said by the form of a mark before it is said by its colour. The coffee idea of the name lives in the ink and the warm neutrals only; there is no coffee-shop decoration.

This file records the Tinto theme, the system this build created, as it ships in the Delivery panel. Four older themes (dark, purple, plum, light) remain in the app and keep their own look; they read the same token names (`--bg`, `--fg`, `--accent`, `--warn`, `--danger` and the rest) with their own values, so a rule written against tokens holds in all five. Only Tinto defines the line colours, the ink window bar and the bundled typefaces.
keyCharacteristics: A transit line diagram as the signature: stages are stations on a solid rail.
One ink for text, primary action, selection edge, focus ring and window bar.
One colour, one job: blue informs and links, green runs and is done, amber is the user's, red broke.
Square corners everywhere; the only round marks are stations and small status dots.
Dense rows, hairlines instead of boxes, borderless secondary controls.
Spanish interface, set in Overpass and Overpass Mono shipped with the app.

rules.name: The Amber Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Amber marks only what waits on the user. A warning nobody has to answer, a blocked task waiting on something else, a note: all neutral.

rules.name: The Red Broke Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what broke. Not emphasis, not a count, not a destructive-looking decoration.

rules.name: The One Colour, One Job Rule
rules.body: Blue is the Agentes line, information and links. Green is the Entrega line, running and done. Ink is action, selection and focus. A colour never takes a second job, which is why the selected row's edge is ink and not green.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Elapsed times, costs and counts use tabular figures and sit at the right edge of their row, so a ticking number never shifts the line.

rules.name: The Middle Dot Rule
rules.body: The interface separates facts on one line with a middle dot. Overpass sets it too tight, so that one character is excluded from the bundled face and falls back to the system font; keep it that way.

rules.name: The One Surface Per Fact Rule
rules.body: A fact is shown in one place. If the line already says it, the row does not repeat it, the header does not restate it and no badge echoes it. Only the selected row shows secondary data; long sections stay folded under a heading with their gist on one line.

rules.name: The Flat At Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface lifts only when it opens on top of the page. Rows, bars, banners and stations never carry a resting shadow.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No rounded corners on controls or containers, at any size. The stations of the stage line and small status dots are the only round marks.

rules.name: The Solid Rail Rule
rules.body: The rail is always solid and continuous. It is coloured only between two passed stations; everything else is grey.

rules.name: The Lit Station Rule
rules.body: A stage under the pointer lights its station and its words. It never gets a grey box.

rules.name: The State By Form Rule
rules.body: Every state has its own shape, so the diagram still reads without colour.

dos: Do keep every control and container square (0 radius), including badges, tooltips, menus and modals.
Do use amber only for what waits on the user and red only for what broke; everything else that is merely noteworthy stays neutral with an icon.
Do show a fact on one surface and fold or remove whatever restates it.
Do draw the rail solid, 4px, coloured only between two passed stations.
Do answer the pointer on a stage by lighting its station and its words.
Do give each state a form of its own before giving it a colour.
Do use ink for the primary action, the selection edge and the focus ring, and keep one primary button per view.
Do separate with hairlines and space, and leave secondary controls without a box.
Do tint shadows and scrims from the ink, and only on surfaces that open on top.
Do write the interface in Spanish and set times, costs and counts in tabular figures.
donts: Don't round a corner. The stations of the stage line and small status dots are the only round marks.
Don't use amber for a warning nobody has to answer, or for a task that is blocked by something else.
Don't use red for emphasis or for anything that did not break.
Don't dash, dot or fade the rail, or colour a stretch that is not between two passed stations.
Don't put a grey box behind a stage under the pointer.
Don't repeat in a badge, a header or a second row what the line already says.
Don't use green for selection, focus or links; green is the Entrega line, running and done.
Don't add coffee-shop decoration: no beans, cups, steam, textures or brown gradients.
Don't rest a shadow under a row, a bar or a banner, and never use a black shadow.
